definitions.explanation: a line running from top to bottom, used in drawing, design, writing, charts, and everyday descriptions

examples.japanese: {縦線|たてせん}を{引|ひ}いてください。
{表|ひょう}の{縦線|たてせん}が{曲|ま}がっている。
examples.english: The vertical lines in the table are crooked.

examples.japanese: グラフに{縦線|たてせん}を{追加|ついか}して、{期間|きかん}ごとの{区切|くぎ}りを{分|わ}かりやすくした。
examples.english: I added vertical lines to the graph to make the divisions between periods clearer.

notes:
Combines {縦|たて} (vertical, lengthwise) and {線|せん} (line). A basic term used in geometry, design, calligraphy, and everyday contexts. Contrasts with {横線|よこせん} (horizontal line).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {縦線|たてせん}を{引|ひ}く: to draw a vertical line
- {縦線|たてせん}と{横線|よこせん}: vertical and horizontal lines
- {太|ふと}い{縦線|たてせん}: a thick vertical line
- {点線|てんせん}の{縦線|たてせん}: a dotted vertical line

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {横線|よこせん}: horizontal line — the counterpart running left to right
- {直線|ちょくせん}: straight line — a line with no curves, not necessarily vertical
- {斜線|しゃせん}: diagonal line; slash — a line running at an angle
